I've used Linux for a few years, and arch for a month. This is my first distro that uses systemd. I'm not a huge fan of it, and from what I read I'm not alone.

I'd like to hear from arch users what they think of systemd. Do you like it? Was it a good switch for arch? Thoughts please.
Systemd: a positive or a plague?

Spreads like a plague, that's certain.

I'm considering hopping over to Gentoo just to experience life without systemd for a while.
It does its job for me, never had an issue. Boot and shutdown times are great. I don't do a lot on my PC outside of games and web browsing, though.

For me, it works.

Is it bloated? Yes. Does it come with things I don't want/need? Yes. Is it sucking up things from Linux that it probably shouldn't? Yes. Would I prefer to have options instead of being strong-armed into using systemd? Absolutely.

But I use it because it is composed (mostly) of things that I'd use anyway, and it comes in the distros that I like to use. Also, it's pretty quick for what it is, and it works pretty well. Yes, it sucks that it's becoming increasingly difficult to get away from systemd, and I wish we had more control over that, but I'm not actually going to take the time to write/compile distros without it, so I can't really complain too much since I don't have a dog in that fight.
I've never actually used anything else day-to-day, but I can't say I really see problems with it.

People only don't like it because they read a bunch of crap about it and how it's "against the Unix way" of pseudo-simplicity (um, GNU is against the Unix way from the start; GNU stands for GNU's Not Unix and was made to basically not be how Unix is, plus tons of basic GNU/Linux tools are anything but "the Unix way").

Plus it's far and away better than anything we've had before. Simple init systems are good for simple OSes like Unix, but when you get to GNU/Linux which can be everything from an embedded system to a full desktop that runs all sorts of things, you need something a bit more complex and that can handle everything in an efficient, simple way.

systemd is the best thing that's ever happened to GNU/Linux. And that's coming from someone that's ran it as my primary OS for about 15 years and have used it personally and professionally for nearly 20.
